general_information.Description: This course examines innovation in stardom, celebrity culture, and social media influence. It explores both tangible and intangible impacts, from disruptive technologies to business model innovation. Students will analyze the evolving dynamics of fame and the interactions that sustain it. The course also investigates the relationship between art and commerce amid digital transformation and the processes and challenges of celebrification faced by traditional celebrities in the digital marketing era.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be eligible for the final examination. - Students are responsible for completing all exercises, questions, and assignments given by the instructor(s)/ lecturer(s) in class or at home and submitting them on time. - Laptops may be used in class solely for learning purposes. - Students must promptly access FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information.

description: This course examines innovation in stardom, celebrity culture, and social media influence. It explores both tangible and intangible impacts, from disruptive technologies to business model innovation. Students will analyze the evolving dynamics of fame and the interactions that sustain it. The course also investigates the relationship between art and commerce amid digital transformation and the processes and challenges of celebrification faced by traditional celebrities in the digital marketing era.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Examine the evolution of stardom and the role of disruptive technologies in shifting fame dynamics from traditional to digital platforms.
Appraise the art-commerce relationship by identifying how business model innovations drive social media influence and digital transformation.
Critique the celebrification process and its associated challenges for traditional celebrities within the current digital marketing ecosystem.
Apply key concepts of digital celebrity and platform influence to analyse how celebrity authority and achievement generate cultural and economic impact in online environments.
Demonstrate professional, ethical conduct, and as well as social responsibility, while collaborating effectively on group projects.

assessments.Grading Guide: Participation is assessed on a 0–10 scale, rounded to one decimal place, and is awarded based on attendance, preparedness, professional learning attitude, and the quality of contributions to class discussions throughout the semester.

assessments.Question Type: Opt.1: Suggested Group Project Requirements Students must form a "Strategic Consulting Group" to produce a Platform Growth Portfolio for a chosen creator. The portfolio must include: 1/ Ecosystem & Archetype Audit Identify the creator’s current standing using Tilton’s Digital Celebrity Taxonomy (e.g., Nanocelebrity, Platform Superstar). Critique the challenges of their "Celebrification" process, specifically analyzing the tension between their "Front Stage" and "Back Stage" 2/ Art-Commerce Innovation Strategy: Design a revenue model using Business Model Innovation Justify how this model preserves "Authenticity" while driving "Social Media Influence." 3/ Theoretical Framework for Influence Justify the strategy using one specific psychological or communication theory from the text: Self-Determination Theory (Autonomy/Competence/Relatedness). Social Identity Theory (In-group/Out-group dynamics). Monroe’s Motivated Sequence (Converting attention to action). 4/ Impact & Ethical Governance: Define 3 KPIs to measure Achievement-based Authority. Draft a Digital Responsibility Manifesto addressing ethical conduct, social responsibility, and transparency Submission Deliverables: A 2,500-word formal report and presentation file (pptx.) Suggested outline: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY [Problem statement, key strategic recommendation, projected outcomes] SECTION 1: ECOSYSTEM & ARCHETYPE AUDIT 1.1 Current Digital Celebrity Standing - Tilton's Taxonomy Classification (with justification) - Platform Presence Matrix (which platforms, engagement metrics) 1.2 Celebrification Process Critique - Front Stage Analysis (public persona elements) - Back Stage Analysis (revealed behind-scenes elements) - Tension Points & Authenticity Risks SECTION 2: ART-COMMERCE INNOVATION STRATEGY 2.1 Current Revenue Model Mapping - Business Model Canvas (9 components visualized) 2.2 Proposed Innovation - New revenue streams or model adjustments - Differentiation from competitors 2.3 Authenticity Preservation Mechanism - How strategy maintains creator's authentic identity - Social media influence leverage plan SECTION 3: THEORETICAL JUSTIFICATION 3.1 Selected Theory (choose ONE): - Self-Determination Theory - Social Identity Theory - Monroe's Motivated Sequence 3.2 Application to Strategy - How theory explains creator's audience relationship - How strategy operationalizes theoretical principles - Predicted outcomes based on theory SECTION 4: IMPACT & ETHICAL GOVERNANCE 4.1 Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) - KPI 1 - KPI 2 - KPI 3 4.2 Digital Responsibility Manifesto - Ethical Conduct Principles (3 commitments) - Social Responsibility Practices (3 actions) - Transparency Mechanisms (3 disclosure policies) SECTION 5: CONCLUSION AI USE DISCLOSURE (if applicable) A short statement indicating whether AI-assisted tools were used. If used, clearly specify: The tool(s) used The purpose (e.g., background research or idea clarification) AI use is optional and must not replace the student’s own analysis. REFERENCES APPENDICES (optional) Opt.2: Follow lecturer's proposal. assessments.Question Type: Opt.1: Suggested Individual Assignment Select one traditional celebrity (film, television, or sports) who has moved into a platform-native space (e.g., YouTube, TikTok, Twitch, personal brand channels). Write a 1500-word critical analysis covering: 1. Technological & Fame Shift: Explain how platform technologies and affordances transform their fame from a top-down media model to a networked, platform-driven model. 2. Platform Economy & Art–Commerce: Analyze how their digital presence connects to monetization systems (ads, sponsorships, subscriptions, brand collaborations) and how this shapes their celebrity identity. 3. Celebrification Challenges: Critically discuss key challenges such as: • Authenticity pressures • Constant visibility demands • Loss of gatekeeper protection • Platform dependence 4. Identity & Boundary Management: Examine how they manage public vs. private identity and image control in digital spaces. 5. Overall Evaluation: Assess the success and limitations of their digital transition. Suggested outline EXECUTIVE SUMMARY [Brief overview of celebrity, platform transition, and key findings] 1. TECHNOLOGICAL & FAME TRANSFORMATION 1.1 Pre-Platform Fame Profile 1.2 Platform Technologies Adopted 1.3 Shift from Top-Down to Networked Fame Model 2. PLATFORM ECONOMY & ART-COMMERCE DYNAMICS 2.1 Revenue Model Analysis 2.2 Brand Collaboration Patterns 2.3 Impact on Celebrity Identity 3. CELEBRIFICATION CHALLENGES 3.1 Authenticity Pressures 3.2 Visibility Demands & Burnout Risk 3.3 Loss of Gatekeeper Protection 3.4 Platform Dependence Vulnerability 4. IDENTITY & BOUNDARY MANAGEMENT 4.1 Public-Private Boundary Strategies 4.2 Image Control Mechanisms 5. OVERALL EVALUATION 5.1 Success Indicators 5.2 Limitations & Risks 5.3 Future Trajectory Assessment 6.
